foods.name: beet powder
notes: [open-datasets] Spoonful: moderate, serving-dependent; trace coloring amounts unlikely to matter.

foods.name: carob powder
aliases: carob bean gum (locust bean gum, e410)
notes: [open-datasets] Spoonful rates carob moderate fructans; locust bean gum thickener is a different fraction and not flagged.

foods.name: casein
notes: [open-datasets] Protein fraction with negligible lactose; not flagged by any FODMAP source. Note: not lactose-free strictly but practically low.

foods.name: celery seed
notes: [open-datasets] Spoonful lists celery/celery seed moderate (mannitol); celery powder is also a nitrite source in 'uncured' meats - small amounts.

foods.name: chicory root fiber
notes: [open-datasets] Inulin source; high at most serving sizes (Spoonful, theibsdietitian, Monash label blog). Alternate label names: chicory root extract, chicory root fibre.

foods.name: citric acid
notes: [open-datasets] Low (gautham50050).

foods.name: fructooligosaccharides
notes: [open-datasets] Short-chain fructans; Monash 'definite avoid'. Common in 'prebiotic' sodas, bars, infant formula, probiotics.

foods.name: galactooligosaccharides
notes: [open-datasets] Monash 'definite avoid regardless of quantity'. Added to prebiotic products and some infant formula.

foods.name: gelatin
notes: [open-datasets] Low (gautham50050).

foods.name: guar gum
notes: [open-datasets] Not rated in sources reviewed; partially hydrolyzed guar gum (PHGG) is actually used therapeutically in IBS. Flag as untested, likely low.

foods.name: inulin
notes: [monash-public] Purified fructan; even very small amounts contribute significantly.

[open-datasets] Pure fructan; high in every source and a Monash 'definite avoid regardless of position in ingredient list'. Added to yogurts, protein/granola bars, cereals, plant milks, fiber supplements, low-sugar chocolate. Even 2 g FOS/day provoked symptoms in IBS (Wikipedia FOS article). OFF ingredient tag en:inulin.

foods.name: lupin flour
notes: [open-datasets] Monash label blog: avoid. Used in some gluten-free and high-protein breads/pasta.

foods.name: milk solids
notes: [open-datasets] Concentrated lactose sources listed by Monash label blog. Ubiquitous in chocolate, biscuits, instant coffee, sauces, crumbed products.

foods.name: natural flavors
notes: [open-datasets] Unclassified; Spoonful notes savory products may hide garlic/onion under 'natural flavors', though amounts under 2% are unlikely to matter. Flag in savory snacks, not sweet ones.

foods.name: pectin
notes: [open-datasets] Low (gautham50050). Jam setting agent.

foods.name: polydextrose
notes: [open-datasets] Synthetic glucose polymer fiber; not FODMAP-classified in any public source reviewed (Monash label blog omits it; fodzyme/gourmend do not rate it). Fermentable and osmotic at high doses; common in 'high fiber' bars and sugar-free products. Flag as untested. OFF tag en:e1200.

foods.name: soluble corn fiber
notes: [open-datasets] Not rated by any public FODMAP source reviewed; partially fermentable fiber used in protein bars/cereals. Flag as untested.

foods.name: soy lecithin
notes: [monash-public] Not formally tested; considered low because it is fat-based and used in tiny amounts.
[open-datasets] Emulsifier; low (Spoonful lists soy lecithin among low soy derivatives).

foods.name: vegetable powder
notes: [open-datasets] Monash label blog: vegetable powders/dehydrated vegetables 'often contain garlic/onion' - treat as fructan risk in savory packaged foods.

foods.name: wheat starch
notes: [open-datasets] Highly refined starch with little fructan; gautham50050 rates moderate, Monash generally treats small amounts low. Position in ingredient list matters.

foods.name: whey
notes: [open-datasets] Lactose depends on processing: whey powder/concentrate moderate (Spoonful, gautham50050); whey protein isolate is low and sold FODMAP-certified. OFF tag en:whey.

foods.name: xanthan gum
notes: [open-datasets] Low (gautham50050; standard GF baking ingredient).

foods.name: yeast extract
notes: [open-datasets] Vegemite/Marmite low at 1 tsp (oseparovic, kwpav, melaniehuang). Not a FODMAP source itself but stock cubes containing it usually also contain onion.

foods.name: beer
foods.lowServing: 1 bottle/can: 12 oz (Kaiser, MNGI), 375 ml (CDHF), 'one' (IBS Diets); ACG/CUH/Glos/Kate/FE: low
notes: [clinical-handouts] Despite being wheat/barley-based, fermentation leaves beer low FODMAP at one serving. Alcohol itself is a gut irritant (Glos, IBS Diets).
[literature] Yao 2014 beer sorbitol 0, mannitol 0; CNF 2943 regular beer fructose 0, glucose 0 -> low. [excess fructose = 0 - 0 = 0.00 g/100 g; cutoff 0.15 g/serve] [oligo cutoff 0.2 g/serve]

[open-datasets] Fructans in barley/wheat are largely fermented out; low at 375 ml per several dietitian summaries of the Monash app. Contains gluten. Community datasets disagree: oseparovic low, ts-sz/gut-check 'moderate', nathaliatg 'high' - the dietitian sources are the better-supported reading. Carbonation and alcohol are gut irritants independent of FODMAPs.

foods.name: brandy
notes: [open-datasets] Low at 30 ml (A Little Bit Yummy, FODMAP Everyday, theibsdietitian).

foods.name: cocktail
foods.lowServing: spirit + soda water, lime, or sucrose-sweetened tonic
foods.highServing: cocktails with fruit juice, agave (margarita), honey, rum, or HFCS syrups (CUH)
notes: [clinical-handouts] Group inferred from typical ingredients.

foods.name: cream liqueur
notes: [open-datasets] Untested. Contains cream (lactose) and sugar; lactose-sensitive users should flag. Not in any public dataset.

foods.name: dessert wine
notes: [clinical-handouts] Residual fructose. Avoid in Stanford, GastroClinic, Kaiser, CDHF, CUH, Glos.
[monash-public] Tested high; FAQ attributes sweet/low-GI wine to fructose.

foods.name: dry sherry
notes: [open-datasets] ts-sz/gut-check list dry sherry as low at a small glass; only one community source, treat with caution.

foods.name: fruit liqueur
notes: [open-datasets] Untested. High sugar; some use HFCS or fruit juice concentrates. A Little Bit Yummy warns sweetened spirits may contain HFCS, honey, agave or sugar alcohols.

foods.name: gin
notes: [literature] Yao 2014 gin sorbitol 0, mannitol 0 -> low. [oligo cutoff 0.2 g/serve]
[open-datasets] Low in every source. Pink/flavored gins may add fruit or sweeteners.

foods.name: gluten-free beer
notes: [open-datasets] Low in every source that lists it (ts-sz, CDHF, nathaliatg). Check label for added fruit juice or honey.

foods.name: hard cider
notes: [clinical-handouts] Apple-based; not explicitly listed in these handouts but apple juice is universally high. Group inferred.

foods.name: hard seltzer
notes: [open-datasets] Untested. Typically fermented cane sugar or vodka plus natural flavor; check for fruit juice concentrate, HFCS or sugar alcohols. Carbonated.

foods.name: ice wine
notes: [open-datasets] Dessert wine; high excess fructose (A Little Bit Yummy citing NUTTAB sugar data, kerenreiser).

foods.name: marsala
notes: [open-datasets] Listed with port as a high-fructose dessert wine by FODMAP Everyday.

foods.name: mead
notes: [open-datasets] Fermented honey; residual honey sugars give excess fructose. Inferred, untested.

foods.name: mulled wine
notes: [open-datasets] Untested. Usually red wine plus sugar or honey, orange and spices; honey-sweetened versions carry excess fructose.

foods.name: non-alcoholic beer
notes: [open-datasets] Untested. Fermentation may be arrested earlier so residual fructans could be higher than regular beer; some brands add sugar or juice.

foods.name: pear cider
notes: [open-datasets] Pears are high in fructose and sorbitol; inferred high, untested.

foods.name: port
notes: [open-datasets] Fortified wine with high residual fructose - high per theibsdietitian and FODMAP Everyday; ts-sz 'moderate' at a small glass.

foods.name: premixed alcoholic drink
notes: [open-datasets] Ingredient-dependent: fruit juice, HFCS and sugar alcohols are common. Flag for label check.

foods.name: red wine
foods.lowServing: up to 250 ml (<100 ml/day in Mediterranean post)
notes: [monash-public] Group not stated in public post.
[open-datasets] Low at 150 ml. A Little Bit Yummy notes excess fructose becomes limiting at larger serves.

foods.name: rose wine
notes: [open-datasets] Low at 150 ml (kerenreiser, ts-sz, theibsdietitian).

foods.name: rum
notes: [clinical-handouts] Only spirit consistently listed high (Kate, Kaiser, IBS Diets, MNGI, CDHF, CUH, Glos, ACG, FE). Group inferred (fructose from sugarcane processing per Monash).
[literature] Yao 2014 rum sorbitol 0, mannitol 0 -> low. [oligo cutoff 0.2 g/serve]
[monash-public] Tested high in FODMAPs; group not stated publicly.

[open-datasets] Every dietitian source reports Monash rates rum high in excess fructose (sugarcane/molasses base). ts-sz/gut-check lists rum 'low' - treat that as an error. Spiced/flavored rums add sugar.

foods.name: sake
notes: [open-datasets] Junmai sake low at 85 ml per FODMAP Everyday (Monash). Sweet/nigori styles untested.

foods.name: sherry
notes: [open-datasets] Sweet/fortified sherry is high in fructose per Monash-derived summaries (theibsdietitian, kerenreiser).

foods.name: soju
notes: [open-datasets] CDHF lists soju under drinks to avoid (fructose), without a serving. No other source; treat as unverified.

foods.name: sparkling wine
notes: [open-datasets] Low at 150 ml in A Little Bit Yummy, FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz. CDHF lists 'sparkling wine' as avoid (fructose) - a minority view, likely referring to sweet sparkling styles. Carbonation is a separate irritant.

foods.name: spirits
notes: [monash-public] Non-FODMAP triggers post: spirits low FODMAP (rum is the tested exception). Alcohol is a gut irritant.

foods.name: stout
notes: [open-datasets] Not separately reported; beer class tested low. Untested style - flag rather than assume.

foods.name: sweet wine
notes: [open-datasets] Higher residual sugar (35-120 g/L) means excess fructose. ts-sz rates 'moderate' at 1 glass; FODMAP Everyday, kerenreiser and CDHF rate dessert wines high. Alcohol also slows fructose absorption.

foods.name: tequila
notes: [open-datasets] Agave sugars are fermented and distilled away; low per Monash-derived summaries (gold and silver both listed by FODMAP Everyday). Mezcal not separately tested.

foods.name: vodka
notes: [clinical-handouts] Low in every source. Watch mixers (fruit juice, regular soda with HFCS, tonic is fine).
[literature] Yao 2014 vodka sorbitol 0, mannitol 0 -> low. [oligo cutoff 0.2 g/serve]
[open-datasets] Distilled; low in every source. Flavored vodkas may contain added sugars/juice - check.

foods.name: wheat beer
notes: [open-datasets] Not separately reported in any public source; beer generally tested low. Treat as beer but flag as untested.

foods.name: whiskey
notes: [literature] Yao 2014 whiskey sorbitol 0, mannitol 0 -> low. [oligo cutoff 0.2 g/serve]
[open-datasets] Low in every source (distillation removes fructans from grain mash). Honey- or flavored whiskeys are different products.

foods.name: white wine
notes: [monash-public] Non-FODMAP triggers post: wine low FODMAP; alcohol itself is a gut irritant. FAQ: "low GI" sweet wines are high in fructose.
[open-datasets] Low at 150 ml in all sources. Dry styles have less residual sugar than sweet.

foods.name: coconut water
